passages.title: Job advertisement and application email
passages.body:
HARBOR LOGISTICS — Warehouse Supervisor

Harbor Logistics seeks an experienced warehouse supervisor for its Rotterdam facility. Responsibilities include managing a team of 25, scheduling shifts and ensuring compliance with safety rules. Requirements: five years of experience in warehousing, including two in a supervisory role; fluency in English and Dutch. Salary: €52,000 to €58,000, depending on experience. Apply by March 15 to careers@harborlogistics.example.

- - - - - - - - - -

To: careers@harborlogistics.example
From: Tomas Wieczorek
Date: March 9
Subject: Application — Warehouse Supervisor

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to apply for the warehouse supervisor position. I have worked in warehousing for seven years, the last three as shift leader at Baltic Freight in Gdansk, where I managed a team of 18. I speak English and Polish fluently and am currently studying Dutch; I expect to reach a professional level by summer. My résumé is attached. I would be available for an interview at any time.

passages.title: Article and letter to the editor
passages.body:
CITY COUNCIL APPROVES NEW DOWNTOWN PARKING FEES

The Millbrook City Council voted 6-3 on Monday to introduce paid parking in the downtown area from July 1. Drivers will pay two dollars an hour between 8 A.M. and 6 P.M., Monday to Saturday. Revenue is expected to fund improvements to bus services. Residents of the downtown zone may apply for a permit costing forty dollars a year. Councilor Ann Lee said the measure would reduce traffic and encourage public transportation.

- - - - - - - - - -

LETTER TO THE EDITOR

The new parking fees will harm the very businesses the council claims to support. Many small shops depend on customers who stop for only a few minutes. Charging them two dollars an hour will push shoppers toward suburban malls. If the council really wants to help downtown, it should offer thirty minutes of free parking and invest first in better bus routes before charging drivers.

Robert Haines, owner, Haines Hardware

passages.title: Article, statement and customer review
passages.body:
LOCAL BAKERY RECALLS GRANOLA BARS

Bakehouse Foods has recalled its Honey-Almond granola bars after discovering that some packages may contain traces of peanuts not listed on the label. The affected bars carry expiration dates between March 1 and March 31. No illnesses have been reported.

- - - - - - - - - -

STATEMENT FROM BAKEHOUSE FOODS

"The safety of our customers is our top priority. We have stopped production of this item until our packaging process is reviewed. Customers who bought the affected bars can return them to the place of purchase for a full refund. For questions, call 1-800-555-0118."

- - - - - - - - - -

CUSTOMER REVIEW — posted March 12

★★★★★ I bought two boxes of Honey-Almond bars last week and love the flavor. After hearing about the recall, I checked the date on my boxes: March 15. I'm taking them back today. I appreciate how quickly the company informed us, and I'll definitely buy their other products.
